To solve the equation \((x! - (x-3)!) \div 23 = 1\), we start by simplifying the expression inside the parentheses. The equation can be rewritten as:

\[x! - (x-3)! = 23\]

We know that \(x!\) (x factorial) is the product of all positive integers up to \(x\), and \((x-3)!\) is the product of all positive integers up to \(x-3\). Therefore, we can express \(x!\) as:

\[x! = x \times (x-1) \times (x-2) \times (x-3)!\]

Substituting this into the equation, we get:

\[x \times (x-1) \times (x-2) \times (x-3)! - (x-3)! = 23\]

We can factor out \((x-3)!\) from both terms on the left side of the equation:

\[(x-3)! \left( x \times (x-1) \times (x-2) - 1 \right) = 23\]

Since \(x-3\) is a positive integer, \((x-3)!\) is a positive integer. The only way the product \((x-3)! \left( x \times (x-1) \times (x-2) - 1 \right)\) can equal 23 is if \((x-3)! = 1\) and \(x \times (x-1) \times (x-2) - 1 = 23\). The only factorial that equals 1 is 1, so we have:

\[1 \times (x-3)! = 1 \implies (x-3)! = 1\]

This means \(x-3 = 1\), so \(x = 4\). We can verify this solution by substituting \(x = 4\) back into the original equation:

\[4! - (4-3)! = 24 - 1 = 23\]

And dividing by 23 gives:

\[\frac{23}{23} = 1\]

So, the value of \(x\) is \(\boxed{4}\).
